subject: ETH
name: Ethiopia
note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. IDs are TL:<subject>:<measure>:<vintage> and stable across builds: a changed value under the same ID is an upstream revision (recorded in the ledger at /ledger); a new observed year is a new claim. A null or absent figure mints no claim — absence is never zero. Scheme: https://terralore.co/integrity

claims.title: Lucy lives in the Afar region
claims.summary: An Australopithecus afarensis individual, later catalogued AL 288-1, lives in what is now the Afar region; her fossilised skeleton would become one of the most famous evidences of early human ancestry.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-3200000bce-lucy-lives-in-the-afar-region, claim TL:ETH:event:3200000bce:lucy-lives-in-the-afar-region, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the kingdom of D'mt
claims.summary: The kingdom of D'mt emerges in the northern highlands, the region's first organised state, blending indigenous and South Arabian cultural elements with its centre near Yeha.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-980bce-rise-of-the-kingdom-of-d-mt, claim TL:ETH:event:980bce:rise-of-the-kingdom-of-d-mt, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Great Temple of Yeha built
claims.summary: A monumental temple dedicated to the moon-god Almaqah is raised at Yeha, reflecting close contact with Sabaean culture across the Red Sea.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-700bce-great-temple-of-yeha-built, claim TL:ETH:event:700bce:great-temple-of-yeha-built, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Transition toward Aksum
claims.summary: D'mt declines and the northern highlands fragment into smaller states, out of which the Kingdom of Aksum would consolidate by the first century CE.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-100bce-transition-toward-aksum, claim TL:ETH:event:100bce:transition-toward-aksum, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Aksum emerges as a trading empire
claims.summary: Aksum consolidates control of the northern highlands and the Red Sea port of Adulis, growing into a major commercial power linking Rome, Arabia and India.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-100-aksum-emerges-as-a-trading-empire, claim TL:ETH:event:100:aksum-emerges-as-a-trading-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Aksum issues its own coinage
claims.summary: Aksumite kings begin minting gold, silver and bronze coins, among the first African states to do so, advertising the kingdom's wealth and reach.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-270-aksum-issues-its-own-coinage, claim TL:ETH:event:270:aksum-issues-its-own-coinage, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: King Ezana adopts Christianity
claims.summary: Ezana converts to Christianity, reportedly under the influence of Frumentius; his coins replace pagan emblems with the cross, making Aksum one of the world's earliest Christian states.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-330-king-ezana-adopts-christianity, claim TL:ETH:event:330:king-ezana-adopts-christianity, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Aksumite intervention in Arabia
claims.summary: Aksum sends forces across the Red Sea into Himyarite South Arabia, the high-water mark of its power before trade routes and the rise of Islam begin its decline.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-525-aksumite-intervention-in-arabia, claim TL:ETH:event:525:aksumite-intervention-in-arabia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Decline of Aksum
claims.summary: The rise of Islam and the loss of Red Sea trade erode Aksum's wealth; the kingdom contracts and its centre of gravity shifts inland and southward.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-700-decline-of-aksum, claim TL:ETH:event:700:decline-of-aksum, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zagwe dynasty established
claims.summary: The Zagwe dynasty takes control of the Christian highlands, ruling from Roha (later Lalibela) and sustaining the Christian kingdom after Aksum's fall.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-1137-zagwe-dynasty-established, claim TL:ETH:event:1137:zagwe-dynasty-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rock-hewn churches of Lalibela carved
claims.summary: King Lalibela commissions eleven monolithic churches cut from the rock to form a symbolic 'New Jerusalem', among the wonders of medieval Christian architecture.

sources.label: Rock-Hewn Churches, Lalibela — World Heritage Centre

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-1200-rock-hewn-churches-of-lalibela-carved, claim TL:ETH:event:1200:rock-hewn-churches-of-lalibela-carved, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Solomonic dynasty restored
claims.summary: Yekuno Amlak overthrows the last Zagwe ruler and founds the Solomonic dynasty, which would rule Ethiopia almost continuously until 1974, claiming descent from Solomon and the Queen of Sheba.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-1270-solomonic-dynasty-restored, claim TL:ETH:event:1270:solomonic-dynasty-restored, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Compilation of the Kebra Nagast
claims.summary: The national epic the Kebra Nagast is set down in Ge'ez, codifying the Solomonic descent of Ethiopia's emperors and the tradition of the Ark of the Covenant at Aksum.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-1314-compilation-of-the-kebra-nagast, claim TL:ETH:event:1314:compilation-of-the-kebra-nagast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Invasion of Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi
claims.summary: Forces of the Adal Sultanate under Ahmad 'Gran' invade the highlands, devastating churches and nearly destroying the Christian kingdom before being repelled with Portuguese aid in the 1540s.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-1529-invasion-of-ahmad-ibn-ibrahim-al-ghazi, claim TL:ETH:event:1529:invasion-of-ahmad-ibn-ibrahim-al-ghazi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fasilides founds Gondar
claims.summary: Emperor Fasilides makes Gondar his permanent capital, beginning the Gondarine period and the building of the Fasil Ghebbi castle complex.

sources.label: Fasil Ghebbi, Gondar Region — World Heritage Centre

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-1636-fasilides-founds-gondar, claim TL:ETH:event:1636:fasilides-founds-gondar, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Onset of the Zemene Mesafint
claims.summary: Central royal authority collapses as regional lords seize real power, beginning the 'Era of the Princes' in which emperors at Gondar rule in name only.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-1769-onset-of-the-zemene-mesafint, claim TL:ETH:event:1769:onset-of-the-zemene-mesafint, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tewodros II reunifies Ethiopia
claims.summary: Kassa Hailu defeats the regional warlords and is crowned Emperor Tewodros II, ending the Era of the Princes and launching efforts to centralise and modernise the state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-1855-tewodros-ii-reunifies-ethiopia, claim TL:ETH:event:1855:tewodros-ii-reunifies-ethiopia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Siege of Magdala and death of Tewodros
claims.summary: A British military expedition storms Tewodros's fortress at Magdala; the emperor takes his own life rather than surrender, ending his reign but not his unifying legacy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-1868-siege-of-magdala-and-death-of-tewodros, claim TL:ETH:event:1868:siege-of-magdala-and-death-of-tewodros, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Addis Ababa
claims.summary: Menelik II and Empress Taytu establish a new capital, Addis Ababa ('New Flower'), which becomes the permanent seat of the empire and later a diplomatic hub of Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-1886-founding-of-addis-ababa, claim TL:ETH:event:1886:founding-of-addis-ababa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Wuchale signed
claims.summary: Menelik signs a treaty with Italy whose divergent Amharic and Italian texts spark a dispute over whether Ethiopia had become an Italian protectorate—setting the stage for war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-1889-treaty-of-wuchale-signed, claim TL:ETH:event:1889:treaty-of-wuchale-signed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Adwa
claims.summary: Ethiopian forces under Menelik II decisively defeat an invading Italian army at Adwa, the first major victory of an African state over a European colonial power and a guarantee of Ethiopian independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-1896-battle-of-adwa, claim TL:ETH:event:1896:battle-of-adwa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Addis Ababa
claims.summary: Italy recognises the full sovereignty and independence of Ethiopia, abrogating the Treaty of Wuchale, though it retains the separate coastal colony of Eritrea.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-1896-treaty-of-addis-ababa, claim TL:ETH:event:1896:treaty-of-addis-ababa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Italian occupation and liberation
claims.summary: Fascist Italy seizes Addis Ababa after the 1935 invasion and occupies Ethiopia, but never settles it as a colony; in 1941 British and Ethiopian forces expel the Italians and Haile Selassie, crowned emperor in 1930, returns and restores independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-1936-italian-occupation-and-liberation, claim TL:ETH:event:1936:italian-occupation-and-liberation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Revolution overthrows the monarchy
claims.summary: The Derg deposes Haile Selassie, ending the Solomonic dynasty after seven centuries; a Marxist military regime under Mengistu Haile Mariam takes power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-1974-revolution-overthrows-the-monarchy, claim TL:ETH:event:1974:revolution-overthrows-the-monarchy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The great famine
claims.summary: Drought, civil war and Derg policies cause a famine that kills several hundred thousand to more than a million people; rights groups attribute much of the toll to government counter-insurgency tactics rather than drought alone.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-1983-the-great-famine, claim TL:ETH:event:1983:the-great-famine, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of the Derg and a new federal order
claims.summary: The EPRDF captures Addis Ababa and Mengistu flees into exile, ending the civil war and the Derg; a new ethnic-federal constitution follows, and Eritrea votes for independence in 1993, leaving Ethiopia landlocked.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-1991-fall-of-the-derg-and-a-new-federal-order, claim TL:ETH:event:1991:fall-of-the-derg-and-a-new-federal-order, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Tigray War
claims.summary: War erupts between federal forces and the Tigray People's Liberation Front, killing an estimated 380,000–600,000 people through combat, starvation and lack of medical care before the Pretoria agreement of November 2022 halts hostilities.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ethiopia: A cradle of humankind and one of the world's oldest states, never colonised, from Aksum to the modern federal republic.", terralore.co/country/ETH/chronicle#ev-2020-the-tigray-war, claim TL:ETH:event:2020:the-tigray-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
